key_insight: Dense user embeddings can be understood as sparse superpositions of interpretable behavioral modes.
engineering_relevance: A post-hoc, model-agnostic interpretation layer can enable natural-language audience retrieval and characterization without changing the upstream embedding system.
method: Model user embeddings as sparse combinations of behavioral modes.
Recover modes using sparse dictionary learning, including sparse autoencoders.
Automatically name recovered modes and query them in natural language.
evidence_signal: Synthetic ground-truth tests show better mode recovery with sparse autoencoders than classical sparse baselines, including for transformer-encoded embeddings; applications span two real-world datasets.
watch_item: The superposition account is approximate for deep representations, so recovered modes and their labels require validation before operational use.
paper_title: User Embeddings are Superpositions of Interpretable Behavioral Modes
